implementation_notes: The platform primitive is the signal: AbortSignal.timeout(ms) returns a signal that aborts with a TimeoutError DOMException after the budget, and AbortSignal.any([parent.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(remaining)]) combines the caller's cancellation with the local deadline - exactly a hop's algebra. Nothing propagates automatically, so every call boundary must forward the signal (fetch(url, { signal }), undici, streaming APIs); the classic hand-rolled setTimeout plus controller.abort() is replaced by timeout()/any(). Note the two documented caveats: an AbortSignal.timeout timer cannot be cancelled early, and long-lived signals keep memory alive while abort listeners are attached, so create signals per call and remove listeners.
idiom_name: AbortSignal.timeout / AbortSignal.any threaded through call boundaries
pitfalls: AbortSignal.timeout is based on active time and never cancels its timer when the operation finishes; long timeouts with abort listeners delay garbage collection, so prefer per-call signals and remove listeners.

AbortSignal.any does not unsubscribe or abort its source signals: aborting the combined signal leaves the parent alive, and the parent's later abort only reaches children that were given the combined signal explicitly.
Code that ignores the signal (CPU loops, libraries without signal support) is not interrupted - the mechanism is cooperative.
The abort reason differs by source (TimeoutError vs the caller's own reason), so inspect e.name/reason to tell budget expiry from user cancellation.
